P1 and P2 are concrete and auditable, but P3 is not yet sound. Defining 0 as “nothing known” conflates no difficulty with missing knowledge, yet permits a reduced seat set when all dimensions are 0—the riskiest interpretation. “Committed on the card” also lacks a canonical schema and checker location, inviting inconsistent records and false positives. I would vote Yes if P3 defines 0 as a positively assessed absence of difficulty and specifies one machine-checkable record format and path.

Clear metrics, counter-metrics, and exit criteria keep the added ceremony bounded.

coach.cite: Dimensions of Difficulty becomes a three-card trial with checkable anchors
coach.reply_head:
Yes

The amendment is proportionate: it preserves independent review while allowing a declared reduced seat set only for cards assessed as difficulty-free. The four dimensions create a practical trigger for adding the perspectives a card actually needs, without padding every task force by default. The three-card trial, Ready failure conditions, committed evidence, metrics, and counter-metrics make P3 inspectable and reversible. P1 and P2 address demonstrated failures with modest ceremony. The remaining odd-seat driver split is correctly escalated rather than smuggled into this patch.

coach.cite: A gate starts on a fresh binary and a clone
coach.reply_head:
Support-it

The amendment answers every round 1 objection to P3. The anchors are checkable, the score line has a committed path a `git show` can print, the Ready check fails a card with absent scores, and only a 2 fires a prescription. P1 and P2 rest on card 324 evidence, and the P1 fix costs about 3 seconds for the build.

On sizing, the reduced seat set for all-0 cards trims ceremony. Keeping the independent gate reviewer and the fresh sign-off keeps the needed perspectives. My reservation is that the 10-minute Ready scoring target could grow into padding, so the counter-metric must be watched. Three parts in one patch is also a lot, though each part has its own metric and trial window.
